Inference

Source: vignettes/articles/Multirates_inference.Rmd
Multirates_inference.Rmd
library(PEPI)
library(dplyr)

We fit PEPI on the polyclonal dataset generated in vignette("Data_generation") and shipped with the package: a wild-type population switching between the “-” and “+” epistates, in which a driver (mutant B) is acquired by a “-” cell. Cells are sorted by epistate and sequenced at two time points, and the population is counted at the same times.

The parameters used to simulate the data are:

truth = c(
  "lambda_n" = 1,
  "s_epi" = 0.5,
  "s_driver[1]" = 0.35,
  "omega_p_wt" = 8e-3,
  "tmrca" = 0,
  "t_driver[1]" = 4,
  "omega_p_driver[1]" = 4e-2,
  "omega_n_driver[1]" = 0.3
)

The data 

data("forest")
data("muts")

The phylogenetic forest of the sampled cells, restricted to the branches of 50 random cells per sample, coloured by species (left), and with the driver branch and the truncal node highlighted (right). Below, the pairwise and marginal VAF spectra of the four sorted samples, with the same labels.

PEPI:::plot_data(forest, muts, seed = 31)

From the data to the model input

The model input is built from the population sizes of the “-” and “+” compartments at the two sampling times, the number of mutations on the driver branch, and the CCF of the driver in the four sorted samples. Population sizes and mutation counts are perturbed with measurement noise.

data("counts")
data("muts")
data("forest")
data("mu")

# The two sampling times.
sampling_times = c(
  counts$sampling_time_1 %>% unique(),
  counts$sampling_time_2 %>% unique()
)
t1 = sampling_times[1]
t2 = sampling_times[2]

# Fraction of "-" and "+" cells in the two samples.
ccf = forest %>% filter(!is.na(sample)) %>% group_by(epistate, sample) %>%
  summarize(n = length(cell_id)) %>% group_by(sample) %>% mutate(n = n/sum(n))

# Total population size at the two sampling times...
z1 = counts %>% filter(time == t1) %>%
  group_by(epistate, mutant) %>% summarize(count = max(count)) %>%
  pull(count) %>% unique() %>% sum()

z2 = counts %>% filter(time == t2) %>%
  group_by(epistate, mutant) %>% summarize(count = max(count)) %>%
  pull(count) %>% unique() %>% sum()

set.seed(31)

# ... measured with lognormal noise.
z1 = exp(rnorm(n = 1, mean = log(z1), sd = 0.2))
z2 = exp(rnorm(n = 1, mean = log(z2), sd = 0.2))

zminus = c(z1, z2) * (ccf %>% filter(epistate == "-") %>% pull(n))
zplus = c(z1, z2) * (ccf %>% filter(epistate == "+") %>% pull(n))

# The driver is the first cell of mutant "B": its branch carries the
# mutations accumulated from the root to the driver acquisition.
driver_id = forest %>% filter(mutant == "B") %>% pull(cell_id) %>% min()
driver_branch = PEPI:::get_branch(forest, cell_id = driver_id, stop_id = 0)

m_driver = muts %>% filter(first_cell_id %in% driver_branch) %>% nrow()
m_driver = rnbinom(n = 1, mu = m_driver, size = 100)

# Driver CCF in the four sorted samples, from the VAF of the driver
# mutations (VAF 1-, VAF 1+, VAF 2-, VAF 2+).
ccf_dr = 2 * (muts %>% filter(first_cell_id %in% driver_id) %>%
  dplyr::select(Sampling_1_N.VAF, Sampling_1_P.VAF,
                Sampling_2_N.VAF, Sampling_2_P.VAF) %>%
  reshape2::melt(id.vars = NULL) %>%
  group_by(variable) %>% summarize(v = mean(value)) %>% pull(v))

The prior on the driver “+” → “-” switch rate is derived from the data:

# Gamma prior on the "+" -> "-" switch rate of the driver, from a plausible
# range of values. The growth rate is bounded above by the growth of the
# total population (log-linear fit of noisy counts above 1e5 cells) and below
# by the growth of the driver "+" cells between the two samples.
z = counts %>% group_by(time) %>% summarize(tot = sum(count)) %>%
  filter(tot > 1e5)

z$tot = exp(rnorm(n = length(z$tot), mean = log(z$tot), sd = 0.2))

fit = lm(log(tot) ~ time, data = z)

lambda_max = coef(fit)[["time"]]
lambda_min = log((zplus[2] * ccf_dr[4]) / (zplus[1] * ccf_dr[2])) / ((1 + 2) * (t2 - t1))

s_max = 2
s_min = 0.1

# ratio of driver "-" and "+" cells at the second sample
rho = (zminus[2] * ccf_dr[3]) / (zplus[2] * ccf_dr[4])

omega_max = rho * lambda_min * s_max
omega_min = rho * lambda_max * s_min

omega_gamma = PEPI:::fit_gamma_quantiles(omega_min, omega_max, p1 = 0.05, p2 = 0.95)
omega_gamma
#> $shape
#> [1] 2.950961
#> 
#> $rate
#> [1] 8.491413

The tables required by init_multirates():

tables = list(

  population_sizes = tibble(
    time = sampling_times,
    type = "sampling",
    zminus = zminus,
    zplus = zplus
  ),

  # the wild type is the complement of the driver
  wt_ccf = tibble(
    time = rep(sampling_times, each = 2),
    epistate = rep(c("-", "+"), 2),
    ccf = 1 - ccf_dr
  ),

  driver_muts = tibble(
    driver_id = "B",
    m_driver = m_driver,
    ms_driver = -0.8,
    sigma_driver = 0.9,
    alpha_n_driver = omega_gamma$shape,
    beta_n_driver = omega_gamma$rate,
    alpha_p_driver = 0.3,
    beta_p_driver = 6
  ),

  driver_ccf = tibble(
    driver_id = "B",
    time = rep(sampling_times, each = 2),
    epistate = rep(c("-", "+"), 2),
    ccf = ccf_dr
  )
)

x = init_multirates(tables, m_trunk = 0)
tables

Inference

fit_multirates() samples the posterior with Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (NUTS) via cmdstanr: here 4 chains with 1000 warmup and 5000 sampling iterations each. Convergence is assessed in vignette("Convergence_diagnostics").

x = fit_multirates(
  x,
  seed = 31,
  chains = 4,
  parallel_chains = 4,
  ndraws = 5000,
  adapt_delta = 0.99,
  max_treedepth = 15,
  init = rep(list(list(omega_p_wt = 3e-3, omega_p_driver = 3e-3)), 4),
  mu = mu$mean,
  l = 51e06,
  t_min = -20,
  ms_epi = -0.8,
  sigma_epi = 0.9,
  alpha_lambda = 10,
  beta_lambda = 10,
  alpha_n_wt = 1,
  beta_n_wt = 1e4,
  alpha_p_wt = 0.2,
  beta_p_wt = 10,
  min_kappa = 3000,
  max_kappa = 5000,
  min_sigma_count = 0.05,
  max_sigma_count = 0.15,
  include_poisson = 1,
  include_trunk = 0
)

Posterior summary, next to the values used to simulate the data:

x$inference$multirates$summary(variables = names(truth)) %>%
  mutate(truth = truth[variable]) %>%
  dplyr::select(variable, truth, mean, median, sd, q5, q95, rhat, ess_bulk)

Prior vs posterior

Prior (transparent) and posterior (solid) distributions; dashed lines mark the values used to simulate the data.

x = get_posterior_multirates(x)

plot_prior_posterior(x, params = names(truth), truth = truth)

Posterior predictive checks

get_predicted_trajectories() simulates new data from the posterior along a time grid. For every draw, the latent “-” and “+” sizes of each population are computed from the model; each population then gets a lognormal total count and a beta “+”/“-” split, as in the likelihood, and CCFs are evaluated on the sampled counts within the “-” and “+” samples. Observed data are shown in red.

pred = get_predicted_trajectories(x)

Fraction of “+” cells in the whole population and total population size:

plot_fractions(x, pred)

plot_counts(x, pred)

Two different fractions describe each population kk (wild type, driver). The first is the fraction of its cells in the “+” state, Zk+/(Zk−+Zk+)Z^+_k / (Z^-_k + Z^+_k): how the population itself is split between the two epistates.

plot_split(x, pred)

The second is the fraction of each sorted sample made of the population, i.e. its CCF in that sample: Zk−/∑jZj−Z^-_k / \sum_j Z^-_j in the “-” sample and Zk+/∑jZj+Z^+_k / \sum_j Z^+_j in the “+” sample. In each sample these fractions sum to 1 over the populations.

plot_ccf(x, epistate = "-", pred = pred)

plot_ccf(x, epistate = "+", pred = pred)
